name: Intuit Inc.

profile.description: Intuit Inc. provides AI-powered financial management, compliance, and marketing products through four segments: Global Business Solutions (QuickBooks), Consumer (TurboTax), Credit Karma, and ProTax. The company serves consumers, small businesses, and accounting professionals, generating ~$21B in FY2026 revenue. In May 2026, Intuit announced a 17% workforce reduction (~3,100 employees) to restructure around AI, including winding down Mailchimp operations and establishing partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Intuit has executed multiple transformative pivots over 40+ years — desktop to cloud, standalone products to integrated platform, and now SaaS to AI-native [1]. The Credit Karma acquisition ($8.1B, 2020) is producing 23% YoY revenue growth. However, the Mailchimp acquisition ($12B, 2021) is being wound down — a significant capital destruction event that prevents a perfect score [3][4]. QuickBooks Online Accounting grew 22% in Q3 FY2026, and Online Ecosystem revenue increased 19% [1]. AI Deployment (2/2): CEO Goodarzi states 'a majority of what we deliver today is fueled by AI,' with QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue growing 22% driven by AI-powered features [1]. Intuit secured multi-year partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI to feed specialized tax and financial data into Claude and ChatGPT, creating advanced generative tools [4]. AI is deeply integrated across TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Credit Karma — inseparable from core revenue. Market Share (2/2): TurboTax dominates U.S. consumer tax preparation, QuickBooks is the clear leader in SMB accounting software, and Credit Karma is the largest free personal finance platform — triple category leadership serving 100M+ users [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): FY2026 guidance of $21.34-21.37B (13-14% growth) with segment-level visibility: Global Business Solutions +15%, Online Ecosystem +19% [1]. AI partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI signal next-gen AI-native products, but specific launch timelines for new AI products are not disclosed. R&D Intensity (1/1): Aggressive R&D investment in AI, demonstrated by laying off 3,100 non-AI roles to hire AI talent and establishing multi-year partnerships with leading AI labs [3][4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Intuit's mission to 'Power prosperity around the world' is specific, aspirational, and connects financial software to human economic empowerment [1]. The mission has guided decades of strategic decisions: TurboTax democratizes tax filing, QuickBooks empowers small businesses, Credit Karma provides free financial access. It is clearly lived and shapes product direction. However, it has not been validated through a true existential crisis that would prove it transcends any single business model. Community Impact (0/2): No specific charitable foundation, community investment programs, or measurable philanthropy was identified in research beyond general corporate recognition awards. Employee Retention (0/2): Two rounds of massive layoffs in consecutive years — 1,800 employees (10%) in 2024 and 3,100 (17%) in May 2026 — represent a devastating ~27% workforce reduction [3][4]. Office closures in Reno, Nevada and Woodland Hills, California compound the disruption. While 16 weeks severance plus career transition services were offered, these layoffs fundamentally undermine any retention narrative. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by CEO Sasan Goodarzi or other executives.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Liquidity floor easily passed: 2,910,152 avg vol x $262.24 = $763M [5]. Every metric scores at or above target. D/E of 36% scores 1.0 — conservative leverage with $6.2B total debt against $3B cash [5]. ROE of 22.5% scores 1.0 (2x weight) — well above the 15% target, reflecting subscription-based software economics [5]. Revenue growth YoY of 13% (FY2026 guidance $21.34B vs FY2025 $18.8B) scores 1.0 [1]. Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of 21.5% scores 1.0 (2x weight) — exceptional compounding from $7.7B in FY2020 [5]. Forward P/E of 10.3 scores 1.0 — well below the 20 target after the stock's ~37% decline from 2025 highs [5]. Profit margin of 21.9% scores 1.0 [5]. Forward PEG of 0.67 scores 1.0 (2x weight) — indicating substantial value relative to growth. All 10 weight units score 1.0. Infrastructure = 10.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Intuit occupies a uniquely precarious position in the AI landscape. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that 'SaaS applications will collapse in the agent era,' directly threatening companies like Intuit whose core products (tax preparation, bookkeeping, personal finance) involve well-structured tasks that AI agents are increasingly capable of performing [3]. Intuit's stock declined ~37% from 2025 highs partly due to AI disruption fears. Free AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini) can already perform basic tax preparation and bookkeeping, creating real substitution risk for TurboTax's DIY tier and QuickBooks' simpler workflows [4]. The company's own 17% workforce reduction to restructure around AI tacitly acknowledges the existential nature of the threat. However, Intuit possesses meaningful defensive moats: proprietary data on 100M+ users, annual tax code complexity requiring specialized compliance, integration with financial institutions, and deep customer switching costs from years of financial history. AI Opportunity (1/1): Intuit generates substantial AI-driven revenue — CEO states 'a majority of what we deliver is fueled by AI,' with multi-year partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI to create specialized financial AI tools [1][4].

infinite_game.summary: Intuit demonstrates a paradoxical infinite game profile. The company has repeatedly reinvented itself over 40+ years — desktop to cloud, standalone to platform, SaaS to AI-native — which reflects genuine existential flexibility. CEO Goodarzi's willingness to bet the company on AI despite divided leadership shows courage. However, two rounds of massive layoffs (27% of workforce in two years) severely undermine the trust foundation that Sinek considers essential. You cannot play the infinite game while treating employees as expendable inputs.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2 pts -> 7/10 display): 'Power prosperity around the world' is a genuine cause validated by decades of strategic decisions — TurboTax democratizing tax filing, QuickBooks empowering small businesses, Credit Karma providing free financial access [1]. The cause has survived leadership transitions and business model transformations. It connects the company's products to meaningful human outcomes. However, it has not reached the NVDA-level of 17-year validation where the purpose IS the competitive advantage.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0 pts -> 2/10 display): Two rounds of devastating layoffs — 1,800 employees (10%) in 2024 and 3,100 employees (17%) in May 2026 — represent approximately 27% workforce reduction in two years [3][4]. Office closures in Reno and Woodland Hills displaced entire teams. The Mailchimp operation is being wound down after a $12B acquisition, representing a broken promise to those employees. While Goodarzi previously demonstrated high-trust leadership (keeping dissenters, encouraging debate), the scale and frequency of layoffs destroy the psychological safety Sinek considers foundational. Remaining employees must operate in an environment of existential job anxiety rather than creative empowerment.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1 pt -> 10/10 display): Goodarzi explicitly acknowledges that AI poses existential risk to SaaS companies, frames ChatGPT and free AI tools as worthy rivals whose capabilities force Intuit to reinvent, and stated 'companies that get disrupted are the companies that just ignore what is happening' [3]. The board appointment of Bill McDermott (ServiceNow CEO, enterprise AI leader) and Adena Friedman (Nasdaq CEO) specifically to bring competitive perspective demonstrates institutional commitment to learning from rivals [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1 pt -> 6/10 display): Intuit has evolved significantly — desktop to cloud, standalone to platform, and now restructuring around AI with Anthropic/OpenAI partnerships [4]. Winding down Mailchimp and cutting 17% of workforce represent dramatic operational changes. However, Sinek distinguishes between flexibility driven by Just Cause and flexibility driven by competitive fear. Intuit's AI transformation appears motivated primarily by fear of disruption ('SaaS collapse') rather than by the Just Cause demanding a new approach to powering prosperity. The changes are significant but not quite the purpose-driven transformative reinvention Sinek celebrates.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1 pt -> 6/10 display): Goodarzi pushed AI transformation when his leadership team was 'absolutely divided,' demonstrating conviction over consensus [3]. The decision to cut 17% of workforce, close offices, wind down Mailchimp, and partner with Anthropic/OpenAI represents a dramatic bet on AI that risks massive near-term disruption for long-term capability [4]. The $300-340M restructuring charge is a real financial cost accepted in service of transformation. However, the courage is directed at survival (avoiding disruption) rather than vision (advancing the cause), which Sinek would note as a finite game motivation.

investment_thesis: Intuit at $262 represents a rare opportunity to own a triple-category leader (TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma) at a forward P/E of 10.3x and PEG of 0.67 — valuations not seen for this franchise in over a decade [5]. FY2026 guidance of $21.34B revenue (13-14% growth) with non-GAAP EPS of $23.80-23.85 reflects sustained profitable growth despite the AI transition headwinds [1]. QuickBooks Online Accounting grew 22% and Online Ecosystem revenue increased 19% in Q3, driven by AI-powered features and higher effective prices [1]. The aggressive restructuring — 17% workforce reduction, Anthropic/OpenAI partnerships, AI-native product transformation — positions Intuit to emerge as an AI winner rather than AI victim. D/E of 36%, ROE of 22.5%, profit margin of 21.9%, and $5B+ free cash flow demonstrate a financial fortress that can fund the transition [5]. The 15% dividend increase to $1.20/quarter signals management confidence in the business trajectory.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on AI disruption risk and cultural destruction. Microsoft's Satya Nadella warned that 'SaaS applications will collapse in the agent era,' and Intuit's core products — tax preparation and bookkeeping — are precisely the well-structured, rule-based tasks that AI agents excel at automating [3]. The stock's ~37% decline from 2025 highs reflects genuine market concern, not mere sentiment. Two rounds of massive layoffs (27% of workforce in two years) and the Mailchimp wind-down ($12B acquisition value destroyed) signal a company in crisis mode, not confident transformation [3][4]. The $300-340M restructuring charge will pressure Q4 FY2026 earnings. Revenue growth decelerated from 17.4% in Q2 to 10% in Q3 FY2026, and Consumer segment growth of 8% lags the company average, suggesting TurboTax — the highest-profile brand — is already feeling AI pressure [1]. The Inspire score of -67 (MISALIGNED) creates an additional screen for faith-aligned investors.
key_catalysts: Valuation re-rating potential at 10.3x forward P/E and 0.67 PEG for a dominant software franchise growing 13%+ — the stock is priced as if AI disruption is certain, creating asymmetric upside if the transformation succeeds [5]

Anthropic and OpenAI partnerships creating specialized financial AI tools that leverage Intuit's proprietary data on 100M+ users — these partnerships could transform Intuit from AI victim to AI platform [4]
QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue accelerating at 22% with AI-powered features driving ARPU expansion and customer retention across the 7M+ subscriber base [1]
key_risks: AI disruption of core tax preparation and bookkeeping products — free AI agents can already perform basic tax filing and bookkeeping, and the 17% layoff implicitly acknowledges the existential scale of this threat [3][4]

Revenue growth deceleration from 17.4% (Q2) to 10% (Q3 FY2026) suggests momentum is fading, particularly in the Consumer segment (TurboTax +8%) which faces the most direct AI substitution pressure [1]

Cultural destruction from 27% cumulative workforce reduction in two years — mass layoffs undermine employee trust, institutional knowledge, and the company's ability to attract top AI talent in a competitive market [3][4]
